title: Steve Eisman Reacts to Scenes From The Big Short
summary: Eisman revisits The Big Short, distinguishes dramatization from his recollection and explains underwriting deterioration, securitization, counterparty exposure and uncertain dealer marks. The most useful material is the research process and the distinction between a correct short thesis and the funding and market structure required to realize it.
assessment: This is a retrospective account, not a new forecast record. Official investigations support the broad underwriting and incentive failures. Some remembered numbers and simplified CDO explanations require correction, while personal meetings, trade dates and dealer conduct are not independently verified by the film or this retelling.
framework_points: Verify an unfamiliar opportunity independently rather than follow a persuasive sales pitch.
Combine loan-level data, field research and institutional exposure mapping.
Ask who holds the other side of a profitable derivative position.
Distinguish an indicative mark from an executable two-way price.
Understand both asset deterioration and the funding system that amplifies it.
tools_and_charts: Dealer bid/ask quotes and valuation marks
transcript_cautions: Automatic captions corrupt names, financial terms and occasional negation. The sentence around 1050 seconds says not only were we wrong despite the surrounding clear claim that the team was right; no thesis is inferred from the isolated caption.
Movie dialogue, Eisman recollection and independent historical evidence are separate sources.
Personal anecdotes without a material financial thesis are summarized rather than treated as forecast claims.
No realized portfolio performance or precise trade record is verified.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman narrates. Embedded movie dialogue is attributed to the film characters and treated as illustrative reported material, not fresh Eisman assertions.

claims.claim: Early subprime securitizations were not uniformly bad; later underwriting deterioration was central to the collapse.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare vintages using consistent age and performance measures.
claims.reason: The official record documents deterioration in later underwriting and loan vintages. It does not mean every early loan was sound or securitization had no other weaknesses.

evidence.title: The subprime lending crisis
evidence.publisher: US Joint Economic Committee majority staff
evidence.finding: The report table gives $231 billion subprime originations in 2002 and $600 billion in 2006, when the share was 20.1%. It documents underwriting deterioration and worse recent vintages. The figures derive from Inside Mortgage Finance and are period-specific.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13
evidence.finding: Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

claims.claim: Lower-rated ABS tranches were sold and then repurchased synthetically to create CDOs, rather than simply remaining unsold.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Separate cash, synthetic and hybrid structures.
claims.reason: Synthetic CDOs referenced securities through swaps, while cash CDOs also owned tranches. Synthetic replication did not require buying the original bonds back. The movie simplification and this universal replacement story are both incomplete.

evidence.title: Story of a security
evidence.finding: The Commission traces both cash deals owning tranches and synthetic/hybrid CDOs using credit default swaps referencing them. A synthetic exposure is not a literal repurchase of the original security.

claims.next_check: Separate cash, synthetic and hybrid structures.

claims.claim: A mortgage ABS is backed by loans, whereas an ABS CDO is exposed to tranches of securitizations.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Read actual collateral schedules and swap documents.
claims.reason: The structural distinction is supported, with synthetic CDOs using contractual references rather than physical ownership.

claims.speaker: Steve Eisman

claims.claim: The team first shorted subprime paper in October 2006.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect dated position and transaction records.
claims.reason: No trade blotter or contemporaneous statement is attached. This reported historical date is not a verified entry price or return.
claims.next_check: Inspect dated position and transaction records.

claims.claim: Dealer-supplied CDS marks could move contrary to worsening loan performance and were less transparent than exchange prices.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare contractual valuation terms, independent quotes and tradeable prices.
claims.reason: The general structure is plausible, but the specific marks and alleged dishonest conduct require transaction records. Divergence alone can also reflect liquidity, model or contract differences.
claims.next_check: Compare contractual valuation terms, independent quotes and tradeable prices.

claims.claim: Goldman changed the valuation method for some positions and supplied a mark materially different from an executable short price.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect contemporaneous valuation notices, quotes and contracts.
claims.reason: Eisman explicitly says he still does not know why this happened. The anecdote does not establish manipulation or an exact bid/ask history.
claims.next_check: Inspect contemporaneous valuation notices, quotes and contracts.

claims.claim: Requesting a two-way market helps test whether a dealer valuation is executable.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Require firm size, validity period and matching contract terms.
claims.reason: A mark is an estimate; a firm bid and offer show the prices at which the dealer will transact for specified size and terms. Wide spreads can be informative without proving fraud.
claims.next_check: Require firm size, validity period and matching contract terms.

assumptions: A two-way quote is firm and applies to the same instrument and size.
proof.derivation: The bid and offer identify executable sale and purchase terms; an isolated valuation does not supply those terms.

claims.claim: FrontPoint risk managers, not Morgan Stanley staff, asked the team to reduce its positions.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect contemporaneous risk correspondence and governance.
claims.reason: This corrects the film narrative but remains personal recollection without inspected risk records.
claims.next_check: Inspect contemporaneous risk correspondence and governance.

claims.claim: Meeting counterparties and issuers was intended to test whether the short thesis was wrong.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Document the strongest opposing evidence and how it changed the thesis.
claims.reason: This is a research principle and recollection; the desired practice is to seek disconfirmation rather than count meetings as proof.
claims.next_check: Document the strongest opposing evidence and how it changed the thesis.

claims.claim: He told Option One that subprime losses would not stop at 5%.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.horizon: Historical 2007 statement, no precise horizon reproduced
claims.test: Recover the contemporaneous statement, portfolio and realized loss series.
claims.reason: This is a retrospective quoted call with an unspecified pool and loss denominator. The audit cannot turn it into a new 2025 forecast or a precise verified historical return.
claims.next_check: Recover the contemporaneous statement, portfolio and realized loss series.

claims.claim: By August 2007 he considered the mortgage market collapse evident in lenders and derivative prices.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare dated market series and contemporaneous records.
claims.reason: The broad deterioration is documented, but his recognition date and portfolio marks are personal recollections.
claims.next_check: Compare dated market series and contemporaneous records.

claims.claim: Morgan Stanley proprietary mortgage exposure produced roughly $10 billion of losses in late 2007.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use the disclosed categories and dates.
claims.reason: The issuer reported $9.4 billion Q4 mortgage-related writedowns, including $7.8 billion US subprime trading positions. Roughly $10 billion is a reasonable rounded recollection, but this was not every bank exposure.

evidence.title: Q4 and full-year 2007 results
evidence.finding: Morgan Stanley reported $9.4 billion mortgage-related Q4 writedowns, including $7.8 billion US subprime trading positions. This supports the large-loss recollection, with the exact amount and reporting period corrected.

claims.next_check: Use the disclosed categories and dates.

claims.claim: A gain on a bilateral derivative means an offsetting contractual loss for the other side.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Trace hedges, collateral and counterparty exposure.
claims.reason: Before fees, defaults and other positions, the two sides of the same contract have opposite cash flows. A counterparty may hedge elsewhere, so this does not identify its net firm loss.
claims.next_check: Trace hedges, collateral and counterparty exposure.

assumptions: One bilateral contract, excluding fees and counterparty failure.
proof.derivation: Every contractual payment from one side is the receipt of the other; their net transfer sums to zero.

claims.claim: The absence of visible loss reports despite profitable shorts prompted him to investigate who held the offsetting exposure.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Map economic exposure across intermediaries and hedge books.
claims.reason: This is a useful investigative question and personal history, not proof that every missing mark was fraudulent.
claims.next_check: Map economic exposure across intermediaries and hedge books.

claims.claim: Bear Stearns failure involved inability to roll funding and emergency support around its sale to JPMorgan.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Distinguish short-term liquidity, asset losses and rescue terms.
claims.reason: The official crisis investigation documents the funding run and rescue. This is a historical explanation, not a fresh collapse forecast.
